description: HydraShield Ground Truth Event Registry — REAL, authoritatively documented hazard events used as benchmark anchors. An event enters this registry only with official sources (meteorological/hydrological services, WMO, Copernicus). The event's occurrence is DOCUMENTED (ClaimStatus vocabulary, src/climate/ontology.py); the expected_signal is what our own datasets (ERA5 reanalysis, GloFAS modelled discharge) should show for that event — it is OBSERVED/MODELLED from the data itself, never restated from the documentation and never fabricated. Events with status key_required declare their missing prerequisite; placeholder events carry no fabricated dates or signals.

status_vocabulary.DOCUMENTED: Event occurrence established in an authoritative report/record (sources cited per event).
status_vocabulary.OBSERVED: Event directly measured by an instrument/authority at the time/place (reserved for instrument-anchored entries).
status_vocabulary.key_required: Event family defined but not executable: a prerequisite (API key) is missing. No fabricated events.

signal_basis_note: Each DOCUMENTED event distinguishes occurrence (DOCUMENTED, from the cited authorities) from signal (OBSERVED/MODELLED, computed from HydraShield datasets). A benchmark never proves the event happened — the sources do. It checks that our detectors reproduce the real signal our own datasets contain for that documented event.

events.name: July 2022 Western-European / UK heatwave (UK 40°C record)
events.signal_basis: Occurrence DOCUMENTED by the UK Met Office (first verified 40°C in the UK, 19 July 2022) and WMO. Expected signal is MODELLED from the ERA5 reanalysis series at the location's own grid point (HydraShield dataset), not restated from the documentation.

sources.name: UK Met Office — Record high temperatures verified (40.3°C at Coningsby, 19 July 2022)
WMO — State of the Climate in Europe 2022 (heatwave assessment)

expected_signal.definition: Heat spell (>=3 consecutive days with daily Tmax above the location's own day-of-year 90th percentile, ±7-day pool, 1991-2020 baseline) detected overlapping the window by >=1 day (heat_percentile_v1 method, src/climate/hazards/heat.py).

events.limitations: ERA5 reanalysis grid point (~25 km) is not the London station record; reanalysis daily Tmax underestimates urban heat islands; the 40.3°C record was set at Coningsby, not London — the signal checked is the multi-day extreme spell, not the absolute record value.

events.name: July 2021 Ahr valley flood (Western Germany)
events.signal_basis: Occurrence DOCUMENTED by DWD (event report on the low-pressure system 'Bernd', 12-15 July 2021) and Copernicus EMS rapid mapping activation EMSR517 (13 July 2021). Expected signal is MODELLED from ERA5 precipitation and GloFAS modelled discharge (HydraShield datasets), not restated from the documentation.

sources.name: DWD — Bericht zu den Starkniederschlägen (Tief 'Bernd'), 21 July 2021
Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping — EMSR517: Flood in Western Germany

expected_signal.definition: Extreme multi-day precipitation in ERA5 (window multi-day totals at the upper end of the location's own ~10-year daily record, 7-day total percentile >=90) AND elevated GloFAS river-discharge percentile (>=90th percentile of the location's own daily series) on >=1 day within the window (flood_discharge_percentile_v1 methods, src/climate/hazards/flood.py).

events.limitations: GloFAS is modelled discharge (~0.1° grid), not a gauge observation of the Ahr; small-catchment flash response is smoothed by reanalysis and hydrological model resolution; the benchmark checks atmospheric + hydrological signal reproduction, not flood extent or impact.

events.name: Storm Eunice (18 February 2022)
events.signal_basis: Occurrence DOCUMENTED by the UK Met Office storm centre (named storm Eunice, red wind warnings 18 February 2022) under the EUMETNET European storm-naming cooperation. Expected signal is MODELLED from ERA5 daily wind-gust maxima at the location's own grid point, not restated from the documentation.

sources.name: UK Met Office — UK Storm Centre (named storms incl. Eunice, February 2022)
EUMETNET — European storm-naming groups (regional cooperation naming storms, incl. the western group: Met Office / Met Éireann / KNMI)

expected_signal.definition: Wind-gust extreme: daily wind-gust maximum at or above the location's own day-of-year 95th percentile (±7-day pool, 1991-2020 baseline) on >=1 day within the window (wind_percentile_v1 percentile machinery, src/climate/hazards/wind.py).

events.limitations: ERA5 reanalysis gusts (~25 km grid) underestimate convective and local extremes; anemometer gusts during Eunice (e.g. 196 km/h Needles, Isle of Wight) are not reproducible at reanalysis resolution — the signal checked is a day-of-year percentile extreme, not the peak gust value.

events.name: Iberian drought, summer 2022
events.signal_basis: Occurrence DOCUMENTED by AEMET (climate monitoring, summer 2022 among the driest on record for Spain) and IPMA (drought monitor: most of mainland Portugal in severe/extreme drought through summer 2022). Expected signal is MODELLED from ERA5 precipitation at the location's own grid point (declared standardized-anomaly method), not restated from the documentation.

sources.name: AEMET — Vigilancia climática (climate monitoring, 2022 drought assessments)
IPMA — Monitorização da seca (drought monitor, Portugal)

expected_signal.definition: Negative 90-day precipitation standardized anomaly: z <= -0.8 for the 90-day window ending 2022-08-31 against same-calendar 90-day windows of the prior ~10 years (drought_anomaly_v1 method, src/climate/hazards/drought.py), AND presence of a dry spell (<1 mm days, >=10 consecutive days) within the window.

events.limitations: Standardized anomaly on a ~10-year same-calendar baseline is a declared screening method, NOT full SPI (no distribution fitting); reanalysis vs station differences; baseline length limits z-score robustness; the drought definition used by AEMET/IPMA (SPI-based) differs from the HydraShield screening method.

events.name: Wildfire event benchmark family (NASA FIRMS-anchored)
events.signal_basis: No occurrence and no signal is declared: wildfire benchmark events derive from real NASA FIRMS detections via src/climate/fire_events.py, which requires FIRMS_MAP_KEY. Until a key is configured and events are derived from real detections, this family carries no events.

sources.name: NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System (API key required)

events.limitations: Requires FIRMS_MAP_KEY; events derive from src/climate/fire_events.py — never fabricated.
